effects.title: Hello, fire
effects.summary: Rising warped noise through the HDR tail. Exists to exercise the foundation end to end.

scorecard.fallback: A static image in the same palette, or a dark CSS gradient.
useCases: Smoke test for the shader pipeline, HDR tail, shell and shared WGSL library
A warm abstract backdrop; it glows, but nothing about it has the shape of a flame yet

effects.title: Advected noise
effects.summary: Ways to make noise look carried by rising gas instead of sliding past as one texture, side by side on the same heat field: scroll, domain warp, flow noise, curl displacement, a two-phase flow blend, and the combination that measures best.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video or animated WebP of the chosen variant; a still frame loses the whole point.
useCases: Choosing how a procedural flame, smoke or ember bed is animated: every variant is one call in advect.wgsl
Seeing what a moving-noise trick costs in noise evaluations before spending it per pixel
A warm abstract fire wall (the backdrop preset) where no flame shape is needed

effects.title: Blackbody colour
effects.summary: Temperature to colour three ways (Planck integral, polynomial fit, lookup texture) with their error, and a brightness mapping tamed enough to use.

scorecard.fallback: A static image of the chart; the colours themselves are available to CSS from the TypeScript twin.
useCases: Colouring a simulated temperature field: blackbody_radiance(t, t_ref, gamma) per pixel
Tinting lights, embers and sparks by temperature without a texture binding (blackbody_tint)
Choosing between the fit and the lookup texture: this scene shows the error of each

effects.title: Bloom tuned for fire
effects.summary: A chart of hot shapes at known radiance, to find how little bloom still reads as heat: threshold, knee, radius, levels, and half against full resolution.

scorecard.fallback: A still image of the chart; it is a tuning tool, not decoration.
useCases: Choosing bloom settings for an effect before spending GPU time on them
Checking that paper white does not glow and that thin, hot detail does
The scene the bloom cost study sweeps `levels` and resolution over

effects.title: Compositing over the page
effects.summary: One flame, smoke and logs written to a see-through canvas five ways: what an overlay effect has to put in alpha to read on a dark page and a light one.

scorecard.fallback: A transparent PNG or WebP of the flame with the same alpha, or nothing: it is decoration.
useCases: Reference for every overlay effect: copy the alpha mode and underlay that suit the page
Checking a theme: switch presets over the dark and the light page to see what survives
A small campfire or hearth decoration that sits on the page instead of in a box

effects.title: Fire as a light source
effects.summary: Wandering flames light a stone page and the cards on it: windowed inverse-square falloff, normal-mapped relief and analytic soft shadows from rounded rectangles.

scorecard.fallback: A static dark image with a warm radial-gradient glow and CSS drop shadows on the cards, offset away from the glow.
useCases: Fire, embers or a cursor torch that lights the DOM cards around it and throws their shadows across the page
Top-down 2D scenes: torches and camp fires lighting a normal-mapped floor
The lighting half of any flame effect: the falloff, shadow and tint functions are a shared chunk

effects.title: Flame colour ramps
effects.summary: One flame through eight colour ramps: blackbody, an authored fire gradient, a banded toon ramp, a blue gas flame and four chemical tints, each as a formula and as a baked texture.

scorecard.fallback: A static image; the same ramps are available to CSS gradients from the TypeScript twins.
useCases: Picking the heat-to-colour mapping for any procedural or simulated flame
Themed fire: copper green, sodium yellow, potassium lilac, lithium crimson, blue gas
Art-directed or banded gradients baked from colour stops into one small texture

effects.title: Flame shaping
effects.summary: One flame at three stages: a teardrop or taper distance field, the heat left after turbulence and erosion, and that heat through the fire ramp.

scorecard.fallback: A static image or a short looping video of the flame; the diagram panels can be a PNG.
useCases: Reference for the shared flame.wgsl chunk: every 2D flame effect starts from these functions
Tuning a silhouette (width, turbulence, erosion, falloff) before building a candle, torch or jet
A single stylised flame for a hero or a card, using the full-frame "flame" view

effects.title: Flicker signals
effects.summary: The shared flicker signal driving three candles, with a scrolling trace of each against the 10% band that defines a flash. Capped by default; the uncapped path is an explicit switch.

scorecard.fallback: The same signal from src/gpu/emission/flicker.ts driving a CSS opacity or filter on a still image; it is plain TypeScript and needs no GPU.
useCases: Intensity and position flicker for any flame, torch, ember bed or firelight on the site, safe by default
One signal shared by a WebGPU flame and the CSS glow around it, so the two stay in step
Checking a flicker setting against the flash threshold before it ships: the trace shows what the cap does to it

effects.title: Heat haze
effects.summary: Rising hot air bends what is behind it: a noise-driven refraction of a backdrop texture, masked by heat, with a faint colour fringe and softening where it is hottest.

scorecard.fallback: The backdrop itself, undistorted, with a still glow at its base. The haze is decoration: nothing is lost without it.
useCases: The air above any flame, ember bed, exhaust or hot surface in a scene the canvas draws itself
Shimmer over a hero image or a video frame uploaded as a texture
Not over live page content: a canvas cannot read the pixels of the DOM behind it

effects.title: Smoke shading
effects.summary: A ray-marched smoke plume lit from below by its fire and from above by a dim sky, comparing three ways to self-shadow it.

scorecard.fallback: A still frame of the plume as a transparent PNG; smoke moves slowly enough that a still reads as smoke.
useCases: Reference for shading smoke in the volumetric fire effects: soot colour, self-shadowing, underlight
A smoke column over a hero or a card, on a dark or a light page (it has real coverage)
Choosing a self-shadowing method by eye: switch `shadowing` between none, gradient and march

effects.title: Soft additive sprites
effects.summary: Embers, sparks and glow puffs as instanced additive quads: procedural shapes, velocity stretch, and the soft-particle depth fade that hides where a sprite cuts through geometry.

scorecard.fallback: A still frame of the scene; sprites alone can also be a CSS radial-gradient per ember on a dark backdrop.
useCases: Embers and sparks rising off any fire, drawn over a 3D scene or over a 2D flame
Glow halos and firelight in haze that must not show a seam where they meet walls and floors
The draw stage of a GPU particle system: the chunk and the renderer take any instance buffer
As drawn here it is an opaque dark scene; additive sprites on their own add nothing to a white page and need a dark region behind them

effects.title: Volume ray-march kernel
effects.summary: An emissive flame and absorbing smoke integrated in one ray march, at reduced resolution, upsampled under the depth buffer so edges against geometry stay sharp.

scorecard.fallback: A looped video or flipbook of the same shot; the march has no cheaper live equivalent.
useCases: The integration kernel under every volumetric fire and smoke effect on the site
A 3D fire that geometry can stand in front of, inside and behind
Choosing step count, march resolution, jitter and upsample filter for a volumetric effect

effects.title: Candle flame
effects.summary: One candle on the page: a teardrop flame with a blue foot, a dark wick and a soft halo over a wax body. It sways on its own and leans away from the pointer.

scorecard.fallback: The poster as a transparent image, or an inline SVG candle with a CSS animation on the flame path; with reduced motion the still frame is the whole effect.
useCases: A memorial, vigil or "lit" state: one calm flame beside a name, a date or a heading
A cursor toy on a landing page: the flame bends as the pointer passes and springs back
A row of tea lights as a quiet footer or loading state, one small canvas each

effects.title: Ember bed
effects.summary: A bed of glowing coals: dark crusts, cracks that breathe, and heat drifting slowly across it. The coal layout is baked once, so a frame is three texture fetches.

scorecard.fallback: The poster: a still of the bed reads the same, since nothing in it moves fast. A CSS radial gradient from dark red to black is the cheapest stand-in.
useCases: A calm, warm background for a hero, a footer or a card, safe to leave running
The base of a fire: put a flame effect above it, or sparks over it
A loading or idle state that should feel warm without drawing the eye
It is an opaque dark picture, so it works on a light page as an image does, in its own box

effects.title: Fire ring
effects.summary: A flame bent round a circle: tongues lick outward or inward from a ring, seamless all the way round, with a progress value that lights only part of it. Transparent in the middle.

scorecard.fallback: A still image of the ring, or a CSS conic-gradient ring with a blur; for the loader, the CSS ring with its own rotation.
useCases: A portal or a summoning circle with page content showing through the middle
A burning frame round an avatar or a badge
A loader or a progress ring: `progress` lights the arc from twelve o’clock clockwise

effects.title: Firelight background
effects.summary: The warm, slowly shifting light of a fire that is just out of frame. No flames: an opaque, calm backdrop for a dark page, steady enough to sit behind text.

scorecard.fallback: A CSS radial gradient in the same colours, which is most of the picture; or a still of the canvas.
useCases: An ambient backdrop behind an article or a hero on a dark page, under a veil and text
A warm fill behind a fire effect that is drawn on top of it
A login or landing screen that should feel lit by a hearth without showing one

effects.title: Fireplace
effects.summary: A whole hearth in one fragment pass: three layers of flame behind charred logs with glowing undersides, firelight on the wall and floor, and embers rising, with no simulation state.

scorecard.fallback: The poster, or a short looping video of the same scene; a still fireplace still reads as one.
useCases: A hero or a card that should feel like sitting by a fire
A cosy background for a landing page, a menu or a holiday banner
A "low evening fire" or "dying embers" idle state: the presets go down to a glow
It is an opaque scene with its own dark room, so a light page shows it as a picture in a box

effects.title: Flame strip
effects.summary: A band of flame tongues along the bottom edge of a wide, short canvas. It repeats exactly once per canvas width, so it tiles at any width, and is see-through above the flames.

scorecard.fallback: A horizontally repeating animated WebP or a short looping video of one period, anchored to the bottom edge; a still of it under reduced motion.
useCases: A section break: a short full-width band of flame between two blocks of content
The top edge of a footer, or the bottom edge of a hero, with the page showing above it
A low ember line under a heading or along the bottom of a card

effects.title: Gas jet
effects.summary: A blue directional flame: a tight cone with a pale inner cone, alone, in a row or as a stove burner seen from above, and with shock diamonds along it for an exhaust.

scorecard.fallback: The poster as a transparent image, or a CSS gradient cone (blue to transparent) with a blurred pale core; the jet barely moves, so a still loses little.
useCases: A burner or pilot light as a state: on, heating, cooking, boosting
Rocket, thruster and afterburner exhausts behind a logo, a ship or a launch button
A blowtorch or welding flame as a cursor trail tip or a progress indicator head

effects.title: Heat-haze overlay
effects.summary: Hot air on its own: an image or a video shimmering in a band, a plume or all over, with no flame in sight. Drop a photo or a video file on it to try your own.

scorecard.fallback: The image or the video itself, undistorted. The shimmer is decoration: nothing is lost without it.
useCases: A hero photograph of a road, a desert, a runway or a grill that should feel hot
The air above an exhaust, a chimney or an engine in a product shot or a video loop
Not over live page content: a canvas can only distort an image, a video or what it draws itself

effects.title: Scrolling-noise flame
effects.summary: The classic: noise scrolled upward, shaped by a height gradient, through a fire ramp. A wall of flame along the bottom edge, with five noise sources to compare.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video or animated WebP of the flame wall with the same alpha; a still poster under reduced motion.
useCases: A wall of fire along the bottom of a hero or a full-bleed section, over the page
A background for a dark landing page, with the flames kept below the headline
Starting point for any 2D flame: the gradient-minus-noise recipe in its smallest form

effects.title: Stateless sparks
effects.summary: Sparks that rise, wobble, cool and die with no buffers and no particle state: each pixel finds its spark from two hashes, in a few depth layers.

scorecard.fallback: Nothing, or a still transparent image of a few sparks: it is decoration and the page loses no meaning without it.
useCases: Embers drifting up behind a dark hero or over a fire drawn by another effect
A welding or grinding spray from a point: a button, a logo, a cursor
Dark pages only. Over a light page a spark is a few pale orange pixels and does not read
Any place a particle system would be overkill: it costs the same with ten sparks or a thousand
The welding spray and grinder presets are over the flash threshold when they fill a large view: keep them small

effects.title: Toon fire
effects.summary: Cartoon fire: three or four flat bands of colour with hard edges and an ink outline, redrawn ten times a second like a hand-animated cel. Opaque paint, so it sits on a light page.

scorecard.fallback: An SVG or a short sprite-sheet loop of the same flame: flat shapes are exactly what those formats are good at.
useCases: A campfire, torch or hazard marker in a game UI or an illustrated page
A flame icon or a streak badge that needs to read at 48 pixels and on a white background
Coloured "magic" fire (the spirit and toxic palettes) where realism would look out of place

effects.title: Torch and brazier
effects.summary: Up to 48 small flames in one canvas, each on a torch or in a brazier and each with its own seed, in a loop that closes exactly. Built to find out what many small flames cost.

scorecard.fallback: A sprite sheet or animated WebP baked from one loop of the effect (it repeats exactly), or the poster as a still.
useCases: List markers, bullets and status icons: many small flames drawn by one canvas laid over the list
A row of wall torches or braziers along a header, a sidebar or a section edge
A seamless loop to bake into a sprite sheet for places WebGPU does not reach

effects.title: Burn front on a fuel map
effects.summary: Burning paper: a sheet over the page that a tap or a stray ember lights. A thin glowing front crosses it, char follows and crumbles, the page shows through the hole, and the sheet grows back.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video with alpha of one burn, or a still of the half-burnt sheet; under reduced motion any frame is a complete picture.
useCases: A cover that burns away to reveal what is under it: a hero image, a spoiler, the next section
A page or route transition, lit from where the visitor clicked
A card or panel that burns when dismissed and leaves the page showing through

effects.title: Reaction–diffusion combustion
effects.summary: Fire as a travelling front in two continuous fields, temperature and fuel. Heat diffuses into unburnt fuel, the fuel ignites and releases heat; the speed and thickness of the front follow from the physical constants. Tap or drag to light it.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video of the fronts crossing with the same alpha, or the still poster; under reduced motion one frame is a complete picture of fronts and char.
useCases: A page or hero that burns: fronts creep over the content, leave char and the ground grows back
Touch-to-ignite surfaces where the fire has to spread at a believable, tunable speed
The reference model to compare a rule-based burn front against: speed, width and extinction come from constants

effects.title: DOM as fuel
effects.summary: The page is the fuel: the rounded rectangles of marked elements are drawn into a fuel map, so fire climbs cards and headings, stops at the gaps between them, leaves a scorch that fades, and the fuel returns.

scorecard.fallback: Nothing: it is decoration on top of real content, which is still there without it. A CSS box-shadow glow on hover is the nearest static stand-in.
useCases: A page that catches fire where it is clicked: a 404, a launch page, a game menu
Cards or headings that burn on a destructive action (delete, dismiss) and come back
Ambient embers smouldering on a dark landing page without hiding its content

effects.title: Doom fire
effects.summary: The PSX Doom heat automaton on a small grid of its own: a bottom row held hot, heat climbing one cell a step. Draw fire with a pointer, let it die and relight it, drive it from scroll or sound.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video or animated WebP of the wall of fire with the same alpha (the pointer drawing is lost); a still poster under reduced motion. The render-pass solver is plain enough to port to WebGL2.
useCases: A wall of fire along the bottom of a hero, a footer or a 404 page that visitors can draw into
Retro and pixel-art pages: the original palette and blocky cells are one preset away
A fire that answers the page: taller while the visitor scrolls, or in time with music

effects.title: Forest-fire automaton
effects.summary: A landscape that burns, regrows and burns again: the Drossel–Schwabl forest-fire automaton on a small grid, with wind, lightning and smoke. Tap or drag to start a fire.

scorecard.fallback: The poster: a still of the map with a fire on it. The rule is a few lines and runs on a 2D canvas at this grid size, so a CPU port is a realistic second step; a looped video cannot be touched.
useCases: A slow, living background for a hero or a section that rewards being left alone for a minute
An interactive piece: visitors start fires with a tap or a drag and watch where the wind takes them
Explaining self-organised criticality, fire regimes or wind-driven spread with something that runs
It is an opaque map, so it works on a light page as an image does, in its own box

effects.title: 3D combustion
effects.summary: Fuel, heat and smoke carried by a 3D stable-fluids solver, burning above an ignition temperature, and ray-marched as blackbody flame and fire-lit smoke over a small scene.

scorecard.fallback: A looped video or flipbook of the same shot (story 8.6), or the 2D grid fire of Epic 6 for a flat view.
useCases: A hero scene with a fire the camera can go round: campfire, brazier, gas burner
Fire that reacts to the scene: wind, a burst of fuel, a burner turned up
The upper bound of what a browser can simulate in 3D within a frame budget

effects.title: Fluid fire
effects.summary: Fire as a fluid: fuel, temperature and soot carried by an incompressible flow, burning above an ignition temperature, lifting by buoyancy and expanding where it burns. Burners, a torch you draw with (press and drag), wood, gas and chemical colours, and the three ways to keep a coarse grid lively side by side.

scorecard.fallback: There is no render-pass version of the solver, so no WebGL2 path: an Epic 4 shader fire (noise-flame, fireplace, gas-jet) or a looping video. Under reduced motion the first frame is already a burning fire.
useCases: A hero or backdrop fire that reacts to a visitor: drag to spray burning fuel, flames that bend round each other
Burners as page furniture: a strip along the footer, a ring round an avatar, a gas jet
The combustion layer later effects reuse (obstacles, heat haze over the page) and the reference for the cheaper fires

effects.title: Fire as page distortion
effects.summary: A hidden heat source below the frame sends a plume of hot gas up through a fluid simulation, and the gas bends the picture behind it: the shimmer rises, curls and fades with the gas instead of scrolling on its own. The pointer is a torch. Drop a photo or a video file on it to try your own.

scorecard.fallback: The picture itself, undistorted, or the noise-driven heat-haze overlay (no compute) for a shimmer that does not follow a flow.
useCases: A hero image above a grill, a radiator or an exhaust whose shimmer should rise and swirl like real hot air
A pointer that warms the page it passes over: text and images waver behind it and settle
Not over live page content: a canvas can only bend an image, a video or what it draws itself

effects.title: Fire round obstacles
effects.summary: Hot gas from a burner under the page rises through a fluid simulation and meets the page as solid walls: the marked cards, headings and buttons. The plume splits round them, curls over their top edges and leaves smoke pooled under overhangs. Press to add heat.

scorecard.fallback: Nothing: it is decoration round real content, which is still there without it. The still poster, or a CSS glow under the cards, is the nearest stand-in.
useCases: A landing page or a 404 whose cards and headings sit in a rising fire and shape it
Showing that a simulation knows where the page is: flow that parts round elements and pools under them
Judging the solver against solids: the SDF test shapes (card row, circle, slanted plate) without a page

effects.title: Stable fluids
effects.summary: The validation scene of the grid-fluid solver ported from Water Temple: smoke and ember glow rising from a smouldering bed, carried by an incompressible velocity field on a staggered grid. Drag to stir it; the controls switch the advection scheme, the pressure solver, vorticity confinement and the grid size.

scorecard.fallback: There is no render-pass version of the solver, so no WebGL2 path: the still poster, or a looping video of the plume. Under reduced motion the first frame is already a plume.
useCases: Checking the solver every Epic 6 effect builds on: schemes, solvers and confinement side by side
Smoke that a visitor can stir, over a dark or a light page
The starting point for combustion: temperature, fuel and smoke in the dye, buoyancy and expansion built in
